title: Establishing a New Team Norm
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article lays out a practical process for deliberately resetting a team's unwritten norms rather than letting them drift. It recommends first making the case for why a new behavior is needed, often by referencing a recent negative episode, then modeling the specific behavior personally before asking others to follow suit. The piece emphasizes introducing one norm at a time, reinforcing it through consistent acknowledgment, and timing the introduction around natural transitions like the start of a new project.
points: Unwritten team norms shape collaboration and decision-making more powerfully than most leaders realize.
Resetting norms in an established team requires deliberately making the case for why a specific new behavior is needed.
Leaders should model the new norm themselves before asking others to adopt it.
The best norms are specific behaviors, not vague guidelines or principles.
Introducing new norms one at a time, and timing them around natural transitions, improves adoption.
quotes: The unwritten rules that guide team interaction are more powerful than most leaders realize.
Good leaders don’t take the powerful influence of norms for granted.
It is not uncommon for leaders to use a recent bad or negative team episode to illustrate the need for the new norm.
The best norms are not guidelines, rules, or principles, but specific behaviors that leaders and team members can learn and enact.
The best leaders introduce new norms one at a time, waiting patiently for the new behavior to take hold before initiating another one.
